root_cause.text: A race in mm/shmem’s shmem_free_swap() read the XArray swap-entry order without holding the XArray lock, so truncate could act on a stale or enlarged multi-page swap entry after it had been split or replaced, freeing/erasing pages past the intended range.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says shmem_free_swap() used xa_get_order “without lock protection” before xa_cmpxchg_irq, allowing an “outdated order value” if the entry was split or changed; the patch fixes this by moving order retrieval and validation into the same xas_lock_irq critical section and by rejecting entries whose computed range “base + nr_pages - 1 > end.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: A race in mm/shmem’s shmem_free_swap() read the XArray swap-entry order without holding the XArray lock, so truncate could act on a stale or enlarged multi-page swap entry after it had been split or replaced, freeing/erasing pages past the intended range.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly says shmem_free_swap() used xa_get_order “without lock protection” before xa_cmpxchg_irq, allowing an “outdated order value” if the entry was split or changed; the patch fixes this by moving order retrieval and validation into the same xas_lock_irq critical section and by rejecting entries whose computed range “base + nr_pages - 1 > end.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix shmem_free_swap() to only remove and free a multi-page swap entry when the entire entry falls within the requested index range.
intent_record.what: The function shmem_free_swap() was changed to take an additional pgoff_t end parameter, replacing a direct xa_get_order()/xa_cmpxchg_irq() sequence with an XA_STATE-based lookup and lock. It now loads the entry at the given index, verifies it matches radswap, computes the number of pages from xas_get_order(), rounds down to the entry's base index, checks that the entire multi-page range lies within [index, end], conditionally clears the xarray slot with xas_store(NULL), and returns nr_pages instead of always returning 1 << order or 0.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this change makes swap freeing aware of the full bounds of a potentially multi-page xarray entry before removing it and freeing swap/cache. It prevents deleting and freeing a large-order swap entry when the requested range only partially covers that entry, avoiding incorrect removal or freeing outside the caller's intended page range. When the whole entry is covered, behavior remains to remove the entry and free the corresponding number of swap pages.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the end-of-range index to shmem_free_swap() in shmem_undo_range() so swap entries are freed correctly within the target range.
intent_record.what: The call to shmem_free_swap() inside shmem_undo_range() was changed from passing three arguments `(mapping, indices[i], folio)` to passing four arguments `(mapping, indices[i], end - 1, folio)`, with only line wrapping adjusted for formatting.
intent_record.how: At runtime, shmem_free_swap() now receives an additional upper-bound/index value of `end - 1`, allowing swap freeing to be constrained or processed with awareness of the range end instead of operating only from the current index and folio. This changes behavior by making swap cleanup range-sensitive in this path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix shmem undo-range handling to correctly skip large swap entries that cross the end boundary instead of retrying them as replaced pages.
intent_record.what: In shmem_undo_range(), the call to shmem_free_swap() was changed to pass an additional end - 1 argument, and when shmem_free_swap() returns 0 the code now declares an order variable, calls shmem_confirm_swap(mapping, indices[i], radix_to_swp_entry(folio)), and skips the entry if it is a large swap entry whose covered range extends past end; otherwise it keeps the existing retry path by resetting index and breaking.
intent_record.how: This changes truncation/undo-range handling for swap-backed shmem so that large swap entries spanning beyond the truncation boundary are recognized and not incorrectly retried as if they were replaced by a page. It allows partial-range handling to leave cross-boundary large swap entries in place after their relevant portion has been zeroed, avoiding wrong retry behavior during execution.

grouping_result.intent: Fix shmem undo-range handling to correctly skip large swap entries that cross the end boundary instead of retrying them as replaced pages.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix shmem undo-range swap handling so multi-page swap entries are only freed when fully within the requested range and are correctly skipped at range boundaries.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly modify shmem_free_swap()/shmem_undo_range() range handling for multi-page swap entries, preventing freeing or erasing pages beyond the intended truncate range at entry boundaries—the same failure mode described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct root cause: it reads the XArray entry order before taking the XArray lock/atomic replacement path, so the order can become stale if truncate or another thread splits/replaces the multi-page swap entry.
This uses the potentially stale order read earlier to free multiple swap slots, which can free beyond the intended entry/range after the entry was split or replaced.
This propagates the stale enlarged order as the number of pages handled, causing callers such as truncate/undo-range logic to skip or erase pages past the intended range.

The caller invoked shmem_free_swap() with only the starting index and no end-boundary information, allowing a multi-page swap entry extending beyond the requested range to be freed based on stale or oversized order.

This call site similarly lacked range-end validation, so if shmem_free_swap() observed a stale/enlarged order it could free a large swap entry crossing the truncate boundary and mis-handle retry logic.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement reads the XArray swap-entry order without holding the XArray lock, creating the race described in the root cause. The resulting stale or enlarged order can later be used after the entry has been split or replaced.
This statement consumes the potentially stale order value to free multiple swap slots, which can free pages beyond the intended truncate range when the multi-page entry has changed concurrently.
This returns the stale multi-page size derived from the unlocked order read, causing callers to believe more pages were handled and potentially skip or erase pages past the intended range.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient to assess the race. In `shmem_free_swap()`, the code reads `int order = xa_get_order(&mapping->i_pages, index);` before performing `old = xa_cmpxchg_irq(&mapping->i_pages, index, radswap, NULL, 0);`. This means the XArray entry order is fetched without first holding the XArray lock protecting the entry state. The root cause describes exactly this pattern: reading the XArray swap-entry order without the XArray lock, allowing truncate to act on a stale or changed multi-page swap entry after it has been split or replaced. Here, the returned page count and the call `free_swap_and_cache_nr(radix_to_swp_entry(radswap), 1 << order);` both depend on that unlocked `order` value. If the entry changes size/order before the locked cmpxchg removes it, `1 << order` may no longer match the actual entry being removed, matching the vulnerable construct. There is no visible fix here such as obtaining the order under the XArray lock / from the locked entry state after successful removal, so the fix is not present.
